newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mother of Israeli baby wounded by bomb is buried.
newsitem.headline: Mother of Israeli baby wounded by bomb is buried.

text.p: Cradling a baby girl in her arms, an Israeli policewoman searched frantically for the infant's mother after an Arab suicide bomber blew up a Tel Aviv cafe.

On Sunday, two days after pictures of six-month-old Shani, clad in a clown costume for the Purim holiday, were seen around the world, the mother was buried to the quiet sobbing of hundreds of mourners.

Coroners were able to identify Anat Rosen-Vinter, 31, as one of the three women killed in the blast only on Saturday, a day after the explosion. Her body had been badly burned by the blast which also damaged the infant's lungs. Doctors said the baby would recover.
"A despicable murderer killed our Anat. She is now on her way to a better place," Zeev Bielsky, mayor of the upscale Tel Aviv suburb of Raanana, said in a eulogy.
He said Rosen-Vinter was a lawyer who joined her father's firm in 1995. She married a dentist four years ago.
"Anat took Shani...and went to enjoy herself a little on this nice, warm day with a girlfriend," her cousin Danny Milo told reporters about the Friday outing to the Apropo cafe.
"(Anat's) mother heard about the (attack)...she had a mother's intuition and checked with all the hospitals."
In an eerie coincidence, another woman named Anat Rosen from Raanana was killed in a bus bombing on Tel Aviv's Dizengoff Street, not far from the cafe, in 1994.
When Shani was born, Rosen-Vinter's mother wrote her hopes for the future in a journal the family decided to keep for the baby.
"I hope you grow up to a world of nothing but beauty...a world of peace and love," Bielsky said, reading the entry, and adding: "It was not to be."
Wrapped in a black shroud, the mother's body was lowered into a grave.
